question: Why do they experiment with RNNs instead of transformers for this task?
title: Combating Adversarial Misspellings with Robust Word Recognition
answer_short: RNNs are preferred for word recognition in this task because they handle sequential data and rare/unseen words effectively, especially with backoff strategies, which is critical for defending against adversarial attacks.
answer_rationale: The evidence indicates that RNNs are used for word recognition in a defense mechanism, suggesting they may be preferred for handling sequential data and rare/unseen words in this specific task context. Specifically, Text 4 and Text 6 highlight that RNN-based semi-character models are employed to predict words from corrupted inputs, and backoff strategies are introduced to handle unseen words. This approach is critical for defending against adversarial attacks, as shown by the accuracy recovery when using RNN-based defenses (e.g., 75% accuracy restored against BERT under attack).
